newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end down on profit-taking.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down across the board on Tuesday on profit-taking triggered by overnight losses on the London Metal Exchange (LME), traders said.
The most actively traded August 1997 contract ended at 23,650 yuan ($2,851) per tonne, losing 250 yuan.
It opened at 23,650 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 23,740 and a low of 23,580 yuan per tonne.
May fell 100 to 23,550, June 190 to 23,610, July 260 to 23,640, September 320 to 23,580 and October 200 to 23,600.
Combined volume fell to 45,490 tonnes from 71,310 tonnes.
Copper opened lower on the LME losses and fell further for most of the session, traders said.

LME copper on Monday failed to hold above the important resistance level of $2,400 a tonne, despite moving up to $2,407 in early trading. By the end of the kerb, the market was at $2,356, down $27 from Friday's kerb close.
Traders in Shanghai said local investors were willing to take profits because of the approach of the Labour Day holiday, especailly as prices approached a key resistance level.
The exchange will close from Thursday to Sunday for the holiday.
"Investors hold different views about overnight losses on the LME and some of the more wary ones liquidated their long positions today," one trader said.
"Many investors are getting cautious as prices approach the key 24,000-yuan resistance level," he said.
Some traders said they believed Tuesday's fall was also a technical correction after Monday's gains and that copper would continue to follow the LME's upward trend in the next few days.
Traders elsewhere in the region, however, saw LME copper falling slowly on Tuesday.
Aluminium ended mostly mixed. May fell 90 to 15,520, June lost 200 to 15,750 and July rose 20 to 16,080.
Combined volume fell to 730 tonnes from 970 tonnes.
